### Repository to remove

https://github.com/epoplavskis/homeassistant_salus

### Why should this be removed?

This repository appears abandoned and is no longer maintained. Users are still discovering and installing it from HACS defaults, then hitting compatibility problems with current Home Assistant / Salus gateway behavior.

Attempts to contact the maintainer and request a deprecation notice have not received a response.

A maintained successor/fork exists here:

https://github.com/Jordi-14/homeassistant_salus
Being maintained by @Jordi-14 and @leonartpitzu

The maintained fork includes current Home Assistant compatibility work and support for newer Salus gateway behavior, including UGE600/UG800 work. It also solves the majority of still open issues in the to-be-removed repo.

### Evidence

- Open issues/PRs unanswered: https://github.com/epoplavskis/homeassistant_salus/issues/     https://github.com/epoplavskis/homeassistant_salus/issues/86     https://github.com/epoplavskis/homeassistant_salus/issues/78
- Maintainer contact attempt: https://github.com/epoplavskis/homeassistant_salus/pull/86#issuecomment-4329813449
- Maintained fork release history: https://github.com/Jordi-14/homeassistant_salus/releases


### Requested outcome

Please remove `epoplavskis/homeassistant_salus` from HACS defaults, or advise on the correct replacement/deprecation process so users are not directed to an abandoned integration.

payload.author: jaycollett
payload.body:
## Repository

https://github.com/jaycollett/OpenIRBlaster

## Category

Integration

## Description

OpenIRBlaster is a Home Assistant custom integration that enables users to learn, store, and replay infrared remote control codes using ESPHome-based hardware.

**Key Features:**
- Learn IR codes from any remote control with a single button press
- Store unlimited codes with custom names, tags, and notes
- One-click replay via Home Assistant button entities
- Full automation support for smart home integration
- Multi-device support for managing multiple IR blasters throughout the home
- Local control via ESPHome (no cloud dependency)

**Use Cases:**
- Control TVs, air conditioners, fans, projectors, and other IR devices
- Create unified dashboards for all IR-controlled devices
- Build automations (e.g., "turn off AC when leaving home")
- Voice control through Home Assistant integrations

**Hardware:**
- ESP8266/ESP32 based
- Includes pre-compiled firmware binary and source
- Circuit diagrams and build instructions provided
- Uses common components (TSOP38238 IR receiver, 950nm IR LED)

**Technical Details:**
- Integrates with Home Assistant's ESPHome integration
- Config flow for easy setup
- Storage of learned codes in Home Assistant storage
- Services for programmatic control
- Entity platform: buttons, sensors, text inputs

**Documentation:**
- Complete README with quick start guide
- Hardware build instructions
- Development and testing documentation
- MIT licensed

**Why HACS Default?**
This integration provides a common, frequently-requested feature (IR control) in a polished, user-friendly package suitable for general Home Assistant users. It eliminates the need for complex ESPHome YAML configurations and provides a unified interface for managing IR codes across multiple devices.

## Additional Information

- **First Release:** v1.0.0 (January 2026)
- **Maintainer:** @jaycollett
- **Home Assistant Version:** 2024.1+
- **Dependencies:** ESPHome integration
- **Issue Tracker:** https://github.com/jaycollett/OpenIRBlaster/issues
- **License:** MIT

The integration has been tested with multiple devices and includes comprehensive error handling, logging, and user feedback.

payload.body:
A Home Assistant integration that connects to a remote server via SSH to collect and display live system metrics. This plugin provides an easy, configurable way to monitor a headless or remote Linux host directly from Home Assistant.

Why It Should Be Included in HACS
1. Remote Monitoring Convenience – It offers a seamless, Home-Assistant-native method for retrieving CPU usage, memory utilization, disk usage, and other vital stats from an external host, removing the need for third-party dashboards.
2. Simple Configuration – Uses a straightforward YAML configuration that requires only SSH credentials and the host’s IP address; no advanced setup or additional software is necessary on the target system.
3. Customizable Sensors – Users can choose which metrics to retrieve, define sensor names, and configure polling intervals for fine-grained control over performance and resource usage.
4. Secure Communication – Relies on standard SSH protocol with public-key authentication (password fallback optional), ensuring a secure channel without exposing additional ports or services.
5. Extensible Foundation – The codebase is modular and well-documented, making it easy to extend in the future with additional sensors or custom features.


Features
- CPU load, memory usage, disk usage, network traffic, and uptime sensors and kore
- SSH-based data retrieval
- Configurable polling intervals
- Support for multiple remote hosts
- Detailed logs for troubleshooting

Dependencies and Compatibility
- Requires Python 3.10+ (matching Home Assistant’s supported Python version).
- Tested with Home Assistant 2023.7 and later.
- Works on Home Assistant OS, Supervised, Container, and Core installations.

- Documentation: https://github.com/404GamerNotFound/vserver-ssh-stats/blob/main/README.md
